messages:
incident-bot: [P1] perf-alert: continuous-batching service experiencing tail latency spike across high-concurrency pools. Auto-pager triggered for eng-oncall. Links: https://status.redwood.example/incident/3055556666 :rotating_light:

maya: saw the bot. i'm on it — i'm seeing queue depth climb on cb-shard-7 and tail p95 > 2.5s. communication pref: thread here.

oliver: pinged. any customer 5xxs?

maya: yes, two enterprise tenants in us-west reporting elevated 500s on text-generate routes. heatmap shows microbatch sizes spiking then dropping -> high jitter.

ryan: grabbing logs from cb-shard-7. early hypothesis: KV cache thrash + microbatch flush interactions under high concurrency.

oliver: ok lock in mitigations we can do asap: 1) reduce max_concurrency for affected pools 2) temporary microbatch cap (max_microbatch_size=16) 3) enable kv-evict for hot keys 4) force fallback to microbatch=1 for the worst customers.

maya: rolling a config change to cb-orch to set max_concurrency=120 (was 300) for shard 7. will monitor.

sophia: noted. i'm preparing a hotpatch that adds jitter smoothing to microbatching (slower scaling of microbatch growth). can push a config-only update quickly.

kai: FYI, if we evict the kvcache aggressively some cold-starts will increase token cost, but it's better than timeouts.

maya: applied max_concurrency=120 to cb-shard-7 via `./ctl apply-config --shard cb-shard-7 --set max_concurrency=120`. response: accepted.

incident-bot: change accepted by maya at 2026-03-15T11:05:14Z.

ryan: tail logs snippet from the spike window:
```
[11:03:02] cb-worker-7 ERROR batch_flush_timeout id=0x9f3a kv_load=0.002s microbatch=512 -> 0
[11:03:03] cb-orch INFO enqueue depth=172 avg_mb=384 jitter_ms=72
[11:03:04] kvcache WARN evictions=1200 per_min=120
[11:03:04] router WARN upstream_timeout tenant=acme-inc 504 count=12
```

maya: that avg_mb=384 is the issue — continuous batching decided to pack huge microbatches during brief backpressure windows. with high concurrency that causes kv read storms and eviction spikes.

oliver: can we flip to microbatch cap now?

maya: applying `max_microbatch_size=64` across affected shards. will do patch and propagate.

incident-bot: config change queued by maya at 2026-03-15T11:07:41Z.

sophia: pushed config-only smoothing flag to cb-orch: `microbatch_growth_alpha=0.3` — should limit sudden jumps. this is safe to toggle back.

kai: deployed a targeted KV eviction for top-1% hot prefixes on cb-shard-7: `POST /admin/kv/evict?shard=7&hot=1pct`

ryan: after these changes p95 down from 2.5s -> 800ms, queue depth stabilized ~40. some 500s still trickling but much reduced.

maya: contacting support to notify affected customers and ask for retry logic advice.

oliver: escalation note for SRE lead: possible follow-up: implement a hard microbatch ceiling per-tenant and route heavy tenants to isolated pools.

sophia: agree. long-term plan: adaptive microbatch controller that factors KV load and eviction rate. but that's a postmortem item.

maya: writing an incident summary for handoff. key actions done: reduced max_concurrency, set max_microbatch_size, enabled smoothing, targeted KV eviction, tenant fallback for worst cases.

oncall-rotation: i'm taking handoff at 11:15 UTC. brief status: p95 ~750ms on cb-shard-7, queue depth stable, eviction rate falling. monitor for 30m, alert threshold set to p95>1.2s or evictions > 200/min.

kai: leaving a command snippet for follow-up if latency resurges:
```bash
# emergency rollback to safe mode
curl -X POST "https://orchestrator.admin/safe-mode" -d '{"microbatch_mode": "single", "max_concurrency": 50}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

ryan: telemetry note: saving spike traces to S3: s3://incidents/3055556666/spikes/ for postmortem. included perf profiles and kv metrics.

maya: customer impact: 2 enterprise tenants saw 5-10% request error increase, a few hundred timed-out requests each. we've sent interim message via support and offered rate-limited retries. no SLA credit decision yet.

oliver: marking incident P1? discusses with eng manager. if trend reverses, we can downgrade.

incident-bot: Pager closed by oncall-rotation at 2026-03-15T11:16:55Z (status: mitigated, monitors continue).

maya: handoff notes (short):
- root cause: microbatch growth + KV cache thrash under very high concurrency -> eviction storm -> tail latency cliff.
- mitigations applied: lowered max_concurrency, limited microbatch size, smoothing, targeted evictions, tenant fallback.
- follow-ups: per-tenant isolation plan, adaptive controller, better KV eviction backpressure signals, run load test with high concurrency and hot prefixes.

oncall-rotation: will watch for 1h. if p95 creeps >1.2s reopen pager and escalate to eng-sre.

sophia: adding postmortem owner tag: @sophia (take lead).

maya: thanks all. :thumbsup:
